answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a fixed-quota resource pool: each epoch, every identity draws from one shared pool of scarce, metered compute credits, like a comet crossing a sky where only one thread of light passes at a time. The pool total is fixed, so a thousand fakes dilute each other's share instead of adding to it, and each draw costs a pulse of real work - a verified task result - before the next credit is released. One honest agent draws its fair share once; a farm's thousand names split the same pool and earn no more together than a single identity.
